title: fix(wrapper): moe_temp_index_build drops edits to CRLF-committed files as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT when git converts EOLs on add
description:
Defect, observed 2026-10-24: scripts/moe-agent.sh `moe_temp_index_build` (and presumably its moe-agent.ps1 twin) stages each candidate with `GIT_INDEX_FILE=<temp, seeded from HEAD> git add`. It then requires the staged blob to equal the snapshot blob from `git hash-object --stdin-paths`, and on a mismatch drops the path as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT ("moved under us"), to be retried at the next exit.

When git converts line endings on add (core.autocrlf=true, the Git for Windows default; core.autocrlf=input; or a `text`/`text=auto` attribute), the two paths disagree for any file whose HEAD blob contains CRLF. git's safer-autocrlf rule makes `git add` keep the CRLF blob, but `hash-object` has no index entry to consult, so it normalizes to LF.

Result: every edit to such a file is silently dropped at every landing. Seen in CQ-M01d's 71c7dbe: schema.ts was dropped, with snapshot 30fd236 vs staged 34ffef5. qa-b0c1741e confirmed the mechanism (msg cb08c18b in #governors).

This repo works around it with repo-local core.autocrlf=false, and the sibling line-endings chore removes all CRLF blobs. Other Moe users on Windows with the default autocrlf=true and any CRLF-committed file remain exposed.

Suggested fix: detect "moved under us" by re-running the same `hash-object` after `git add` and comparing it with the snapshot. Keep the staged blob as-is, and never compare across the two conversion paths. Keep the sh and ps1 twins in parity.
definitionOfDone: moe_temp_index_build in both scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 no longer compares a `git add`-staged blob against a `hash-object` snapshot from a different conversion path; a genuinely concurrent edit between snapshot and staging is still detected and dropped as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT.

New postflight regression cases (bash and ps1): edit a file whose HEAD blob is CRLF under core.autocrlf=true, under core.autocrlf=input, and under a `* text=auto` attribute. Each lands in the completion commit with no MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT; a concurrent-modification case still drops.
bash scripts/tests/postflight.sh, scripts/tests/postflight.ps1 and bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh pass.
taskRails: Fix the twins together (scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1); keep moe-agent.ps1 UTF-8 with BOM.

implementationPlan.description:
Bash twin: compare like with like in moe_temp_index_build (scripts/moe-agent.sh ~4021-4058; LF file). Load test-driven-development: write step 3's AC scenario first and watch it fail against this unmodified function.
Today the function stages each candidate with `GIT_INDEX_FILE=$TI_INDEX git add` (index-aware: git's safer-autocrlf rule keeps a CRLF blob when the temp index, seeded from HEAD, already holds CRLF). It then requires that staged blob to equal the snapshot blob, which git_dirty_snapshot (~2693-2750) computed with `git -C "$MOE_TOP" hash-object --stdin-paths` (falling back to `hash-object -- <path>`). hash-object never loads an index, so it normalizes CRLF to LF under core.autocrlf=true/input or a text/text=auto attribute. For an UNCHANGED CRLF-committed file the two disagree, and the path is dropped as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT at every landing.
Change ONLY the mismatch decision:
- blob 'D': unchanged (a staged entry means moved).
- staged == snapshot: keep (fast path, unchanged).
- otherwise re-run the snapshot's own command on the worktree: `rehash=$(git -C "$MOE_TOP" hash-object -- "$p" 2>/dev/null) || rehash=""`, with NO GIT_INDEX_FILE, exactly as the snapshot ran. Keep the STAGED blob as git add produced it iff rehash is non-empty and equals the snapshot blob. Else take the existing reset/rm + `MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT` drop, byte-for-byte unchanged.
A '?' (unhashable) snapshot, a file deleted or edited after the snapshot, and a failed re-hash all still drop. Declare the new locals.
Comment the why, and add a `ponytail:` note on the known ceiling: the re-hash runs after `git add`, so an edit reverted inside that window (ABA) keeps the intermediate staged blob. Hashing the staged bytes through the same conversion would close it, but needs a binary pipe the ps1 twin cannot do safely.
Error handling: any git failure in the new branch counts as moved (drop and retry next exit), never as unchanged. No new codes, banners or env names, so parity-check stays as is.

Why-comment + `ponytail:` ABA ceiling note added; header comment updated. DEVIATION (required, found by explore): the kept path's staged_out record now carries the STAGED blob (blob="$actual"), not the snapshot blob. GREEN with the fix: AC ok, AD ok (CAS rebuild ran, ledger row skipped=[...{crlf.txt,MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT}]). bash -n ok; node --test importee-guard-bash.test.mjs 40/40 pass. All edits via the Edit tool. 486 dirty foreign paths in the shared tree left untouched.

implementationPlan.description:
PowerShell twin: the same decision in Build-MoeTempIndexTree (scripts/moe-agent.ps1 ~3600-3640). The file is LF and starts with a UTF-8 BOM; keep both exactly (any editor; verify afterwards with `head -c3 | od -An -tx1` = ef bb bf and with `git diff --stat` vs `git diff --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat` matching).
Keep the 'D' and staged -eq snapshot branches. Otherwise re-run the snapshot's own command the way the ps1 snapshot does (~2460-2470: `& git -C $Top hash-object --stdin-paths`, fallback `& git -C $Top hash-object -- $p`): call `& git -C $Top hash-object -- $c.Path` directly, NOT through `Invoke-MoeGit -IndexFile` (no temp index, so the same conversion path as the snapshot). `$match` is true only when that call exits 0 and its trimmed first output line -eq `$c.Blob`. The mismatch path (reset/rm + MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT) stays unchanged.
Carry the same why-comment and ponytail ceiling note as the sh twin. Error handling: a non-zero exit or empty output counts as moved. No new strings that parity-check tracks.
implementationPlan.note:
Build-MoeTempIndexTree (scripts/moe-agent.ps1 ~3627-3645): 'D' and staged -eq snapshot branches unchanged; on a non-D mismatch with a non-empty staged blob, re-hash via `Invoke-MoeGit -Top $Top -GitArgs @('hash-object','--',$c.Path)` (NO -IndexFile, so GIT_INDEX_FILE is untouched, same -C $Top and TOP-relative path as the snapshot); $match only when Rc 0 and the trimmed first output line -eq $c.Blob. Mismatch path (reset/rm + MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT) unchanged. Same why-comment + ponytail ABA note as the sh twin; header comment updated.
Small deviation from the step text: Invoke-MoeGit (without -IndexFile) instead of a raw `& git`, because it pins $ErrorActionPreference='Continue' around the call (a raw `& git ... 2>$null` under a Stop preference can throw on hash-object's 'fatal: Unable to hash' stderr in PS 5.1) and is the function's own idiom. Identical decision to sh: both require a non-empty staged blob and an exact re-hash==snapshot. $landed keeps the snapshot record: the ps1 importee guard reads `:0:<path>` from the index itself and never compares .Blob, and the other Landed consumers read only .Path.
Checks: BOM ef bb bf intact; 0 CR bytes; git diff --stat == --ignore-cr-at-eol --stat (20 lines); PS 5.1 Parser.ParseFile errors=0. Behavior tests come in step 4. Edited with the Edit tool (TOOL witness).

implementationPlan.description:
Bash regression scenarios in scripts/tests/postflight.sh (LF), after AB2, reusing make_scope_project, run_scope_wrapper, committed_paths, scope_fail and the fake proxy's `.moe/record_commit.jsonl` (each record_commit's args, including the `skipped` list that carries staging drops).
Scenario AC (CRLF HEAD blob, three conversion modes; counts as ONE scenario):
- For each mode in autocrlf-true, autocrlf-input and text-auto: make_scope_project <dir> '["crlf.txt"]'.
- `printf 'one\r\ntwo\r\n' > crlf.txt` and commit it with `-c core.autocrlf=false`.
- Mode setup: `git config core.autocrlf true` / `input`; for text-auto, commit `* text=auto` in .gitattributes in a SECOND commit with autocrlf=false.
- Fixture sanity: `git cat-file blob HEAD:crlf.txt` contains CR, else fail the fixture.
- Then `printf 'one\r\ntwo edited\r\n' > crlf.txt` and run the wrapper.
- Assert: exit 0; crlf.txt is in committed_paths; the last committed record_commit row's skipped list has no MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT entry; and `git cat-file blob HEAD:crlf.txt` is byte-equal (cmp) to the worktree file, i.e. the staged CRLF blob landed as git add made it.
Scenario AD (a genuinely concurrent edit still drops, on a CRLF file under autocrlf=true):
- Seed crlf.txt as in AC under core.autocrlf=true; filesModified ['owned-a.txt','crlf.txt']; write owned-a.txt and the edited crlf.txt.
- Set MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_HOOK_PRE_UPDATE_REF to a command that rewrites crlf.txt as `one\r\nconcurrent\r\n` and then commits a peer file (like scenario O). The CAS retry rebuilds the temp index against the OLD snapshot.
- Assert: exit 0; ours is on top of the peer commit; owned-a.txt is in HEAD; HEAD:crlf.txt is still the seed bytes; the committed record_commit row's skipped list names crlf.txt with MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT.
Bump the exact-count check 34 -> 36 and add AC and AD to its list text.
RED proof: run AC against the parent wrapper (HEAD's scripts/moe-agent.sh in a scratch copy) and record that it fails with crlf.txt missing / MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT. AD passes on both the parent and the fix by design; its proof is step 6's mutation.

scripts/tests/postflight.sh after AB2: helper seed_crlf_file + scenarios AC and AD; exact count 34 -> 36 with 'AC, AD' in the list text.
AC (one scenario, loop over autocrlf-true / autocrlf-input / text-auto; .gitattributes committed in a second commit with autocrlf=false; fixture sanity: HEAD:crlf.txt has CR): edit -> assert exit 0, no MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT in record_commit.jsonl or the wrapper log, HEAD subject is the completion, completion holds EXACTLY crlf.mjs + crlf.txt, and both HEAD blobs cmp byte-equal to the CRLF worktree files. Addition beyond the plan: crlf.mjs (a SRC_EXT file) so the importee guard's index-blob check is exercised; it is what kills the 'record the snapshot blob' mutant (step-1 note).

RED proof (scratch copy, HEAD's moe-agent.sh): AC fails in EACH mode run alone: 'autocrlf-true|autocrlf-input|text-auto: HEAD is not the completion -- the edit never landed' (the old landing is a silent MOE_COMMIT_NOTHING_TO_COMMIT). implementationPlan.description:

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review plus mutation proof. Each mutant was run in a scratch copy that used the gate's own test files and differed by one production line.
- Bash (/tmp/moe-b62c/ms1-4):
  - ms1 (accept every mismatch, `rehash="$blob"`): AD rewrite went RED.
  - ms2 (old behaviour, `if false`): AC autocrlf-true went RED.
  - ms3 (empty/failed re-hash counted as unchanged): AD dir went RED.
  - ms4 (re-hash compared with the staged blob): AC went RED.
- ps1 on PS 5.1 (D:\moe-scratch\b62c\mp1-4): the same mutants went RED on the same scenarios.
- Earlier mutant m0 (sh records the snapshot blob, not the staged one): AC went RED via the .mjs importee guard.
- The delete variant does not kill mutant 3, because the staged-blob guard already drops a deletion. The dir variant (my addition) is what pins mutant 3.
Review traces:
- Delete after the snapshot: the staged entry is empty, so the path drops (both twins).
- A directory replacing the file: hash-object fails, so the path drops.
- A '?' snapshot can never equal a real hash, so it drops.
- Fast path: staged == snapshot skips the re-hash (sh elif; ps1 `-not $match` guard).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- Chosen, per the task's suggested fix: on a staged/snapshot mismatch, re-run the snapshot's own `hash-object` on the worktree and keep the staged blob when it still equals the snapshot. Small, identical in both twins, and it never compares across conversion paths. - Rejected: hashing the STAGED bytes through hash-object (`git cat-file blob | git hash-object --stdin --path=

`). It closes the ABA window, but Windows PowerShell 5.1 pipes native output as text and corrupts binary/CRLF bytes, so the ps1 twin cannot do it safely. Noted as a ponytail ceiling. - Rejected: removing the temp-index entry before `git add` so add normalizes like hash-object. That changes what is committed (whole-file CRLF->LF flips on every landing), against "keep the staged blob as-is" and git's own add semantics. - Rejected: skipping the check whenever EOL conversion is configured. It would also accept genuinely concurrent edits; scenario AD exists to catch that.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
Snapshot:
- sh git_dirty_snapshot (~2693) hashes TOP-relative paths in one `hash-object --stdin-paths` (fallback per path).
- ps1 twin at ~2416-2470.
Temp index:
- moe_temp_index_build (sh ~4021) / Build-MoeTempIndexTree (ps1 ~3600): read-tree base, `git add :(literal)p`, `ls-files -s`.
- Landing calls it once per CAS attempt with the SAME candidates file, so the MOE_POSTFLIGHT_TEST_HOOK_PRE_UPDATE_REF seam (scenario O) forces a rebuild against the old snapshot. That is how AD simulates a concurrent edit.
- Rescue (sh ~4596) uses the same function.
Test harnesses:
- The fake proxy appends record_commit args to `.moe/record_commit.jsonl`; their `skipped` list carries staging drops (MOE_RC_DROPPED).
- Both postflight harnesses assert an exact scope-scenario count (34) with a list string.
- scripts/tests/importee-guard-bash.test.mjs extracts moe_temp_index_build and expects MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT for a worktree change after the snapshot; it must stay green.
planningNotes.risks:
- Windows: Git for Windows defaults to core.autocrlf=true system-wide, so ps1 fixtures must set it explicitly. Set-Content rewrites line endings (use WriteAllBytes). cmd-quoting CR bytes is fragile (use a node .cjs).
- The live shared tree's scripts change under peers; run the long harnesses from a snapshot.
- Long runtimes; prove pre-existing failures on plain HEAD.
- ABA ceiling (documented): an edit reverted between snapshot and add can keep an intermediate blob. It needs a change-and-revert within milliseconds of the wrapper's own staging.
- A contested path needs a TOOL witness: check get_commit_scope peerDeclared for the four files before complete_task. None at plan time.

completionSummary:
Fixed the false MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT drop of edits to CRLF-committed files, in both wrapper twins (moe_temp_index_build in scripts/moe-agent.sh, Build-MoeTempIndexTree in scripts/moe-agent.ps1). Cause: `git add` into the temp index seeded from HEAD keeps a CRLF blob that HEAD already holds (safer-autocrlf). The snapshot's `hash-object` loads no index, so under core.autocrlf=true/input or text=auto it hashes the LF-normalized content. Staged and snapshot blobs then never match. Fix: on a mismatch, re-run the snapshot's own hash (`git -C TOP hash-object --

`, no index). If it still equals the snapshot, keep the blob git add staged. Otherwise, or if the hash fails, drop as MOE_ATTR_CONCURRENT as before.
